title: Abundance given, then prayer and sacrifice
translation: We have given you abundance. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. It is the one who hates you who is cut off.
body: Exegetes split on **al-kawthar**. In Muslim, **Anas** reports a river the Prophet was promised; in Bukhari, **Ibn ʿAbbās** calls it “the good” God gave him, and his pupil Ibn Jubayr makes the river part of that good. Gift, then prayer and offering: the **Apology** (XXIV) cites Psalm 116 for thank-offerings by those already reconciled.
question: The surah moves from abundance given to an enemy “cut off”. How might these two images answer each other?
source_label: Bukhari 4966 · Muslim 400 · Apology of the Augsburg Conf. XXIV
